What we make

## Soda, but dirty

A dirty soda is a fountain soda over nugget ice with flavored syrup, fruit purée and a pour of cream. We build every one to order from a mobile trailer, so the Dr Pepper is cold, the coconut cream is real cream and the lime is fresh. 114 drinks on the board, or build your own and show us at the window.

It doesn't stop at soda. We run real soft serve for cones, cups, shakes and floats. The espresso is pulled fresh, not pumped from a box, for iced lattes, cold brew and the sweeter stuff. Lemonades come shaken, Italian sodas come creamy, and the freeze-dried candy is made in house. Kids get their own sizes.

We open first in [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) and southern Utah ([Washington City](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-washington-city), [Santa Clara](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-santa-clara), [Ivins](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-ivins), [Hurricane](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-hurricane-sand-hollow)), and we book events on Utah's Wasatch Front (Lehi, Utah County and the Salt Lake area) and Florida's Gulf Coast (Tampa Bay, St. Pete, Sarasota and Naples). Farmers markets, ball games, church and school events, weddings, company parties. If there's somewhere for a trailer to park, we'll bring the beach to it.

Questions

## St. George dirty soda FAQ

**What is a dirty soda?**

A fountain soda over nugget ice with flavored syrup, fruit purée and a splash of cream. It started in Utah, and Utah's best-known chain started here in St. George. Dr Pepper with coconut and sweet cream is the classic, and our Thirst Trap is exactly that.

**Where is the trailer?**

We're opening soon. St. George is where we open first, and until then we're booking private events in St. George, the rest of Utah and Florida ([get a quote](https://thirstybeaches.com/#events)). Once we're open, the live map on this page shows exactly where we're parked and the stops list shows the rest of the week. Text and email alerts are coming soon.

**Can I book Thirsty Beaches for an event in St. George?**

Yes. Weddings, ward and school activities, team parties, HOA socials and company events across Washington County: [Washington City](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-washington-city), [Santa Clara](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-santa-clara), [Ivins](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-ivins), [Hurricane](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-hurricane-sand-hollow) and [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) itself, from [Desert Color](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-desert-color) to [Green Valley](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-bloomington-green-valley). We also book Utah's Wasatch Front and Florida's Gulf Coast. [Send the date, place and head count](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=St.%20George#quote) and we'll reply with a price within one business day.

**Do you have drinks for kids?**

Yes. The Beach Babies menu is sized and priced for kids, from a Lil' Root Beer Float to a Sandcastle Shake, and soft-serve cones are always a hit. Lemonades and Italian sodas have no caffeine, and most sodas come in a zero-sugar version.

**How much is a dirty soda?**

On our menu, dirty sodas are $3.49, kid sizes are $2.99 to $4.50 and soft-serve floats are $5.95 to $7.50. The whole board runs $2.95 to $9.99; see the [menu](https://thirstybeaches.com/menu) for every price. Events are quoted by guest count and hours.

**Can I build my own drink?**

Always. Use the builder on this page to pick a base, syrup, cream and topping, then show the screen at the window and we pour it exactly like that. You can share the build with a link.

**How do I pay?**

Tap to pay, cards and cash. Once we open you can order at the kiosk or the window, and the punch card on this site earns a free drink after ten.

# Dirty soda in St. George, Utah

> A retro dirty soda trailer opening first in St. George: built-to-order sodas, soft-serve floats and espresso for Washington County weddings and events.

Canonical page: https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · St. George, UT

Opening soon · Booking St. George events now


St. George is where we open first. Dirty sodas built to order, real soft serve and fresh espresso, all out of one retro trailer that comes to you, from Bloomington to Washington City and out to Ivins and Sand Hollow.

[Book a St. George Event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=St.%20George#quote) [See the Menu](https://thirstybeaches.com/menu)

## St. George has soda shops. We're the one that drives to you.

Nobody in St. George needs dirty soda explained. One of Utah's best-known soda chains opened its very first shop here in 2010, and the drive-thru soda line has been part of town life ever since. We're not trying to replace your usual stop. What a drive-thru can't do is roll up to your reception, your ward party or your office parking lot and pour for everyone at once. That's the whole idea of the trailer. Our Thirst Trap is the classic (Dr Pepper, coconut, sweet cream), and from there the board runs to 114 drinks, or you can [build your own](https://thirstybeaches.com/#build) and show us the screen at the window.

## Built for southern Utah heat

St. George gets an early start on summer. Spring shows up while the Wasatch Front is still shoveling, the 90s arrive by May, and July and August run past 100. That's float weather for half the year, and it's what the trailer is built for: every drink over nugget ice, and a real soft-serve machine so any soda can turn into a float, with cones, cups and shakes for anyone skipping the soda. We pull espresso to order too, for iced lattes and sweet-cream cold brew at a 7 a.m. event before the heat sets in. Zero-sugar sodas, caffeine-free lemonades and Italian sodas, and Beach Babies kid sizes cover the whole family.

## Events from Bloomington to Washington City

We built the trailer around the parties St. George actually throws: wedding receptions and backyard open houses in Little Valley, Bloomington and Green Valley, venues out in Ivins and Santa Clara, ward and stake activities, youth nights, missionary farewells and homecomings, birthday parties and graduation open houses. PTA and booster nights at Desert Hills, Snow Canyon, Pine View, Dixie and Crimson Cliffs. HOA and neighborhood socials in Desert Color, SunRiver and Coral Canyon. Club and department socials around Utah Tech, and office treat days and client open houses for the teams at Tech Ridge and around town. See [event packages](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering#packages), or jump to [St. George weddings](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-wedding-soda-bar), [graduations and birthdays](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party), [HOA and neighborhood parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party), [church and school events](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-church-school-events), [tournaments and team parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-tournaments-team-parties) or [company parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-company-party).

## St. George, neighborhood by neighborhood

St. George is a lot of small places stitched together, and each has its own kind of party. Down by the Southern Parkway, [Desert Color](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-desert-color) has a white-sand lagoon, vacation rentals and a community calendar with food-truck nights, so it's rental-house reunions and pool-day birthdays. On the southwest side, [Bloomington and Green Valley](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-bloomington-green-valley) go back to a pioneer settlement on the Virgin River and a ranch that became a resort neighborhood, and the parties are in big backyards and at HOA clubhouses. Out east, Little Valley is tournament country (see [tournaments and team parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-tournaments-team-parties)), and the 55+ communities like SunRiver run clubhouse socials of their own (see [HOA and neighborhood parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party)). Wherever you are in town, the trailer comes to you.

## Dixie Center, Town Square and the big weekends

St. George is a town of big weekends: expos and conventions at the Dixie Center, the St. George Art Festival on Town Square over Easter weekend, marathon and triathlon weekends, Swiss Days in Santa Clara and Peach Days in Hurricane. Running a booth, a vendor row, a team tent or an after-party at one of them? Ask about a pop-up where guests buy their own drinks, or a covered tab for your crew. Venues and city events set their own vendor rules, so we'll check what yours needs before we quote, and we'll only list a public stop once it's actually booked.

## The small towns around St. George

The trailer covers all of Washington County, not just St. George proper, and the towns around it have pages of their own. [Washington City](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-washington-city) and Coral Canyon are next door. [Santa Clara](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-santa-clara) is the old Swiss pioneer town of Swiss Days and Santa Clara Drive, and [Ivins](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-ivins) has Kayenta and the red-rock resorts by Snow Canyon. [Hurricane](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-hurricane-sand-hollow) has Sand Hollow's red-sand beach, and north of it [LaVerkin, Toquerville and Leeds](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-laverkin-toquerville-leeds) are small towns with a lot of history, from the Ash Creek settlement to the Silver Reef museum. Further out, like Winchester Hills, Dammeron Valley, Veyo, Cedar City or Springdale, just ask and we'll put any travel in the quote.

# Dirty soda in Washington City, Utah

> Dirty sodas, soft-serve floats and espresso from a retro trailer for Washington City and Coral Canyon parties, HOA socials and school nights.

Canonical page: https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-washington-city

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) · Washington City

Opening soon · Booking Washington City events now


Washington City is right next door to St. George, where we open first. Dirty sodas built to order, real soft serve and fresh espresso for backyard parties, HOA socials and school nights, from Green Springs to Coral Canyon.

[Book a Washington City Event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Washington%20City#quote) [See the Menu](https://thirstybeaches.com/menu)

## Next door to where dirty soda started

Washington City sits just east of St. George along the Virgin River, and the soda habit here is as strong as anywhere in Washington County. Utah's best-known chain started here, a few miles down the road, and the drive-thru soda run is part of a lot of commutes. We're not a drive-thru. Thirsty Beaches is a retro trailer you book for your own event, and it pours for everyone at once. The Thirst Trap (Dr Pepper, coconut, sweet cream) is the classic, the board runs past a hundred drinks, and you can [build your own](https://thirstybeaches.com/#build) and show us the screen at the window.

## Neighborhood parties from Green Springs to Coral Canyon

A lot of Washington City is newer neighborhoods with an HOA calendar to fill: Coral Canyon out on the east end, Sienna Hills, Washington Fields, Green Springs, and the older streets around Telegraph and the historic downtown. Those are the parties we built the trailer for. A pool-deck social, a block party that deserves better than a cooler of cans, a back-to-school night for the street, a welcome party for the new move-ins. Tell us the head count and whether the HOA is covering the tab, we park on the street or in the clubhouse lot, and everyone gets a drink built the way they like it. Kid sizes and zero-sugar versions keep the whole street happy. More on [HOA and neighborhood parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party).

## Schools, wards and teams on the east side

Crimson Cliffs High School and the elementary and middle schools around it keep the PTA and booster calendar full. We do teacher appreciation days, PTA carnivals, senior nights and team fundraisers, with a caffeine-free menu whenever a school asks for one. Wards and stakes book us for youth nights, ward parties and missionary farewells and homecomings. If your activity is at a meetinghouse, the building's rules come first, so a covered tab with no sales is usually the simplest fit, or we can meet you at a park or a home. See [church and school events](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-church-school-events) and [tournaments and team parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-tournaments-team-parties).

## Made for Washington County summers

Summer afternoons here regularly pass 100 degrees, and an outdoor party needs cold drinks that don't take forever. Every drink is poured over nugget ice, the soft-serve machine turns any soda into a float, and cones and shakes cover anyone skipping the soda. For a midday summer event we'll suggest a short menu and a morning or evening window so nobody waits in the sun. Spring and fall evenings are close to perfect for a backyard party, and that's when a lot of receptions and open houses happen out here. Planning one? See [southern Utah weddings](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-wedding-soda-bar).

## Markets, Cotton Days and community events

Washington City has deep roots. The old cotton factory still stands near the historic downtown, and it's why the town's community celebration is called Cotton Days. The Saturday farmers market at Veterans Park, the community center and the city parks all host events of their own. Organizing a booth, a vendor row or a community night? Ask about a pop-up where guests buy their own drinks. Events and venues set their own vendor rules and permits, so we'll check what yours needs before we quote, and a public stop only goes on our list once it's booked.

## On the way to Quail Creek and Sand Hollow

From Washington City it's a short drive to Quail Creek and Sand Hollow, and plenty of visiting families stay in rentals out this way. Family reunions, cousins in town for the week, a birthday at a rental with a pool: those make great private bookings. If your event is further east, see [Hurricane and Sand Hollow](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-hurricane-sand-hollow). Back across the river, [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) is where the trailer opens first.

# Dirty soda in Desert Color, St. George

> A retro dirty soda, soft-serve and espresso trailer for Desert Color birthdays, rental-house reunions, HOA nights and lagoon-day parties in St. George.

Canonical page: https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-desert-color

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) · Desert Color

Opening soon · Booking Desert Color events now


St. George has a beach, and it's in Desert Color. Dirty sodas built to order, real soft-serve floats and fresh espresso for backyard birthdays, rental-house reunions and neighborhood nights, from a retro trailer that comes to you.

[Book a Desert Color Event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Desert%20Color#quote) [See the Menu](https://thirstybeaches.com/menu)

## A beach inside St. George

Desert Color is the master-planned community along I-15 and the Southern Parkway, on the land east of the interstate. Its centerpiece is the lagoon at The Shores: about two and a half acres of water with more than half a mile of white-sand shoreline, which the community calls the largest private body of water in the St. George area. People swim, kayak and paddleboard there in a desert town. We named the trailer Thirsty Beaches and built it around one idea, bringing the beach to you, so a neighborhood with its own beach is about as close to home as it gets. Utah's best-known chain started in St. George, so nobody here needs dirty soda explained. What we add is real soft serve and fresh espresso in the same trailer, so any soda can become a float and the morning crowd gets an iced latte.

## Rental houses, reunions and pool-day parties

Desert Color has vacation rentals, some with a private pool, and families book them so three generations can stay under one roof for the week. That is a perfect private booking for us: we pull up to the house for a couple of hours, pour for everybody, and the cousins line up for floats. Check your rental's rules on vendors and parking first, and make sure a truck and trailer can pull onto a flat spot nearby. Residents throw the same parties at home: a birthday by the pool, a graduation open house, a welcome party for the family that just moved onto the street. Kid sizes, zero-sugar sodas and caffeine-free lemonades and Italian sodas mean the grandparents and the toddlers both get something.

## The resort side runs its own drinks

The Shores Resort has its own pool-deck café, Atara has its own restaurants, and Crush Golf + Grill has its own dining and private event spaces. Those places run their own food and drinks, so we don't set up at the lagoon, the resort pools or a restaurant without their invitation, and an event held there goes through them first. The community also sets the rules for its pools, parks and amenities. For a lagoon day, the easy version is to meet you back at your home or rental afterward, when everyone is sandy, sunburned and thirsty.

## A neighborhood calendar that never stops

Desert Color runs a busy community calendar of its own. It lists summer kickoff events with food trucks, dive-in movie nights, holiday lights, car shows, pinewood derbies and moonlight 5Ks, and it has its own parks, about six miles of trails and a pickleball park at Akoya Pearl Community Park with six courts, a performing pavilion and an activity lawn. If you sit on an HOA, a neighborhood committee or an event team and want a drink trailer at a community night, talk to whoever runs the event and then to us. Organizers set their own vendor rules, so we'll check what yours needs before we quote. The HOA can cover everyone, set a cap, or let neighbors buy their own. See [HOA and neighborhood parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party).

## Floats on the hottest days

Summer afternoons in St. George regularly pass 100 degrees, and that is exactly when a soft-serve float beats everything else on the board. Every drink is poured over nugget ice, and cones and shakes cover anyone skipping the soda. For a midday summer party we'll suggest a short menu and a morning or evening window so nobody waits in the sun. Morning crowds headed to pickleball get espresso and sweet-cream cold brew; evening crowds get the full dirty soda board.

## Birthdays, graduations and the 55+ crowd

Desert Color has everything from vacation rentals and family homes to a 55+ community, so the parties range from a seventh birthday to a seventieth. Kids want anything blue; grandparents want a caffeine-free lemonade or a Diet Coke with coconut. We'll name a drink after the birthday kid or the graduate and match the syrups to the school colors. See [graduation and birthday parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party). Elsewhere in town, [Bloomington and Green Valley](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-bloomington-green-valley) are on the southwest side, and [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) is where the trailer opens first.

## Where you'll find us in Desert Color

We're not open for public stops yet, and we won't make up a date. Public stops go on the [homepage stops list](https://thirstybeaches.com/#stops) and the live map once they're actually booked, and text and email alerts are coming soon. Until then, the fastest way to get the trailer to Desert Color is to [book it for your own event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Desert%20Color#quote).

# Dirty soda in Bloomington and Green Valley, St. George

> A retro dirty soda and soft-serve trailer for Bloomington, Bloomington Hills and Green Valley backyard parties, HOA socials and family nights, St. George.

Canonical page: https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-bloomington-green-valley

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) · Bloomington & Green Valley

Opening soon · Booking Bloomington and Green Valley events now


The southwest side of St. George, from old Bloomington on the Virgin River to the resort streets of Green Valley. Dirty sodas built to order, real soft serve and fresh espresso for backyard parties, clubhouse socials and family nights, from a retro trailer that comes to you.

[Book a Bloomington or Green Valley Event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Bloomington%20or%20Green%20Valley#quote) [See the Menu](https://thirstybeaches.com/menu)

## Bloomington: the town before the town

Bloomington was a pioneer settlement before it was a St. George neighborhood. The Carpenter family settled the northwest side of the Virgin River and called the place Jamestown; they raised cotton and sugar cane, made molasses and started a broom business. The surveyor renamed it Bloomington, and by the middle of the last century the families were gone. Then a developer began marketing a country club community here, with a golf course at its heart. The Washington County Historical Society calls it the first planned community in Utah and the spark that finally put St. George on the map. Today Bloomington is golf-course streets, the old Manzanita Road settlement and Bloomington Petroglyph Park, all on the river side of town.

## Green Valley: a ranch that became a resort

Green Valley, on the west side of town, started as a six-hundred-acre ranch. Once it was annexed into St. George, the first subdivision went in, and then The Park at Green Valley, which came with an owners association, a clubhouse, a pool and courts at a time when that was new for St. George. The Sports Village, Las Palmas, The Cottages and the Green Valley Spa followed, and condos that were rented to visitors helped make Green Valley a place people come to stay. That mix of long-time owners and visiting families is exactly who books a trailer: a clubhouse social for the residents, or a reunion for the family that rented three condos for the week.

## Backyards, cul-de-sacs and clubhouse lots

The parties we hear about on the southwest side are mostly at home: a birthday in a big Bloomington backyard, a graduation open house in the driveway, a missionary homecoming on the cul-de-sac, a pool-day social at the HOA clubhouse. We need a flat spot that a truck and trailer can pull into, close enough to your guests that the line feels like part of the party. The trailer runs on its own generator and carries its own water, so no hookup is needed. If the HOA owns the clubhouse lot, get its OK first. A party that moves into a public street or a city park can need a city permit, so ask us and we'll walk through it. More on [HOA and neighborhood parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party) and [graduations and birthdays](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party).

## Golf-course neighborhoods and club rules

Country clubs and resorts usually run their own food and drinks, and their event contracts often say so. If your event is at a clubhouse or a resort, check with its events team first; if outside vendors are allowed, we'll work with them on where to park and when to load in. A party at a home on the course is simpler: you decide, as long as your HOA agrees.

## Early tee times and hot afternoons

Southwest St. George mornings start early. We pull espresso to order, so a 7 a.m. group gets iced lattes and sweet-cream cold brew, then the board switches to dirty sodas, lemonades and floats over nugget ice as the day warms up. Summer afternoons regularly pass 100 degrees, so for a midday summer party we'll suggest a short menu and a morning or evening window. Zero-sugar sodas, caffeine-free lemonades and Italian sodas, and Beach Babies kid sizes cover the whole family.

## Wards, schools and the rest of town

Wards and stakes on this side of town book us for youth nights and ward parties, and PTAs and booster clubs book teacher thank-yous and fundraisers. See [church and school events](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-church-school-events). Further south, [Desert Color](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-desert-color) has its own lagoon and community calendar, and out west [Santa Clara](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-santa-clara) and [Ivins](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-ivins) have pages of their own. Back in the middle of it all, [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) is where the trailer opens first.

## Where you'll find us on the southwest side

We're not open for public stops yet, and we won't make up a date. Public stops go on the [homepage stops list](https://thirstybeaches.com/#stops) and the live map once they're actually booked, and text and email alerts are coming soon. Until then, the fastest way to get the trailer to Bloomington or Green Valley is to [book it for your own event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Bloomington%20or%20Green%20Valley#quote).

**Can our HOA book you at the clubhouse?**

Yes, with the HOA's OK. The HOA can cover everyone, set a cap, or let residents buy their own. Tell us what the HOA requires from vendors and we'll confirm we can meet it before we quote.

No. The trailer runs on its own generator and carries its own water. We just need a flat spot a truck and trailer can pull into.

# Dirty soda in Santa Clara, Utah

> A retro dirty soda and soft-serve trailer for Santa Clara, Utah backyard receptions, graduation open houses, reunions and ward parties. Booking events now.

Canonical page: https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-santa-clara

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) · Santa Clara

Opening soon · Booking Santa Clara events now


Old orchards, Swiss pioneer roots and a main street lined with painted cows during Swiss Days. Dirty sodas built to order, real soft serve and fresh espresso for Santa Clara backyard receptions, open houses and family parties, from a retro trailer that comes to you.

[Book a Santa Clara Event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Santa%20Clara#quote) [See the Menu](https://thirstybeaches.com/menu)

## The town the Swiss settlers built

Santa Clara is older than most of the county. It began as the headquarters of Jacob Hamblin's Indian Mission on the Santa Clara River, and then a company of Swiss converts was sent south to settle it. Weeks after they arrived, a long rain flooded the river and destroyed the fort and the first settlement, and the earlier settlers moved over to the land where the Swiss families had settled. The Swiss knew how to grow grapes, and the warm climate turned out to be ideal for fruit; the Washington County Historical Society says Santa Clara became the fruit and vegetable garden of the county, and fruit stayed the town's main living for more than half a century.

## Swiss Days and Santa Clara Drive

The city's Swiss Days celebration honors those Swiss pioneers. The city describes a parade along Santa Clara Drive from the Jacob Hamblin Home to City Hall, pioneer activities at Heritage Square, live entertainment, local food and merchandise vendors, and decorated cows that residents and businesses display along Santa Clara Drive and in their yards. Vendors go through the city's own sign-up. If the trailer is ever part of a Swiss Days weekend, it will be because the city accepted us, and it will go on our stops list then. A private party at your own home is always an easy booking.

## Family parties in a family town

Santa Clara still feels like the small town it grew from, and the parties we hear about here are family ones: graduation open houses, missionary farewells and homecomings, reunions, birthdays and the backyard reception after a wedding. Old orchard lots and big yards usually have room for the trailer. We need a flat spot a truck and trailer can pull into, close to your guests, and the trailer brings its own power and water. Kid sizes, zero-sugar sodas and caffeine-free lemonades and Italian sodas mean the grandparents and the toddlers both get something. See [receptions and open houses](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-wedding-soda-bar) and [graduations and birthdays](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party).

## Wards, schools and teams

Wards and stakes book us for youth nights, ward parties and trek send-offs. Lava Ridge Intermediate is in Santa Clara, and west-side PTAs and booster clubs book teacher thank-yous, carnival nights and team fundraisers. If your activity is at a meetinghouse, the building's rules come first, so a covered tab with no sales is usually the simplest fit, or we can meet you at a park or a home. See [church and school events](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-church-school-events) and [tournaments and team parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-tournaments-team-parties).

## Santa Clara summers

Summer afternoons here regularly pass 100 degrees, so we plan around the heat: a morning open house with iced lattes and sweet-cream cold brew, or an evening party once the sun drops. Every drink is poured over nugget ice, and the soft-serve machine turns any soda into a float. For a midday event we'll suggest a short menu and a time window that keeps the line moving.

## Next door: Ivins and St. George

Santa Clara and [Ivins](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-ivins) are next-door neighbors on the west side of the county, and the trailer covers both. Ivins started out as the Santa Clara Bench, and it has Kayenta and the red-rock resorts. Back toward town, [Bloomington and Green Valley](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-bloomington-green-valley) are on the southwest side, and [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) is where we open first.

## Where you'll find us in Santa Clara

We're not open for public stops yet, and we won't make up a date. Public stops go on the [homepage stops list](https://thirstybeaches.com/#stops) and the live map once they're actually booked, and text and email alerts are coming soon. Until then, the fastest way to get the trailer to Santa Clara is to [book it for your own event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Santa%20Clara#quote).

# Dirty soda in Ivins, Utah

> A retro dirty soda, soft-serve and espresso trailer for Ivins and Kayenta receptions, red-rock backyard parties and family get-togethers. Booking now.

Canonical page: https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-ivins

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) · Ivins

Opening soon · Booking Ivins events now


Red cliffs, black lava and a town that started as the Santa Clara Bench. Dirty sodas built to order, real soft-serve floats and fresh espresso for Kayenta receptions, backyard parties and family get-togethers on the Snow Canyon side, from a retro trailer that comes to you.

[Book an Ivins Event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Ivins#quote) [See the Menu](https://thirstybeaches.com/menu)

## From the Santa Clara Bench to Ivins

Ivins began as farmland on the Santa Clara Bench, settled about a century ago by families descended from Swiss immigrants, who farmed it with water carried by canal from the Santa Clara River. After the chapel was dedicated, the settlers chose to name the town after Anthony W. Ivins, and he agreed on one condition, according to the Washington County Historical Society: that they spell it Ivins, not Ivens. Today it is a growing city near Snow Canyon State Park, and the parties here still tend to happen at home, on a patio with a view of the red cliffs. That is where a trailer beats a drive-thru: we park, we pour for everybody, and nobody loads the kids in the car for a soda run.

## Kayenta and the art village

Kayenta covers about 2,200 acres of Ivins, and most of it borders open space. Its art village has galleries, a café, the Center for the Arts at Kayenta and a desert labyrinth laid out in small stones. It is one of the prettiest places in Utah to throw a reception, a shower or an open house, and a neon-pink trailer looks good in the photos against red rock. Kayenta has its own homeowners association, so check its rules on vendors and street parking before you book, and tell us where the trailer can pull in. More on [southern Utah receptions](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-wedding-soda-bar).

## Tuacahn, Black Desert and the resorts

Ivins is home to Tuacahn Center for the Arts and its outdoor amphitheater, and to resorts including Black Desert, with a golf course laid through the black lava fields, Red Mountain and others. Theaters, resorts and their restaurants run their own food and drinks, so we don't set up there without their invitation, and an event held there goes through the venue first. If you're staying in a rental or a family home nearby, a private party there is easy: check the rental's rules on vendors and parking, and we'll handle the rest.

## Fire Lake Park, Snow Canyon and the heat

Ivins has a beach of its own too: Fire Lake Park at Ivins Reservoir has a beach and a swim area. City parks have their own rules, so for a party at Fire Lake or another Ivins park we'll check what the city needs first. Snow Canyon State Park is on the doorstep, and commercial vendors need the park's permission to sell inside a Utah state park, so for a trailhead group or a race we'll meet you at a home or a private lot nearby instead. Summer afternoons pass 100 degrees, so we plan morning events with iced lattes or evening parties after the rock cools off, all over nugget ice.

## Heritage Days, schools and wards

The city holds its own Ivins Heritage Days, and organizers set their own vendor rules, so ask the city before you picture us there; we only list a public stop once it's booked. Red Mountain Elementary is in Ivins, and west-side PTAs and booster clubs book teacher thank-yous and fundraisers. Wards and stakes book youth nights and ward parties. See [church and school events](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-church-school-events).

## Next door: Santa Clara and St. George

Ivins and [Santa Clara](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-santa-clara) sit side by side on the west edge of Washington County, and the trailer covers both. Back toward town, [Bloomington and Green Valley](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-bloomington-green-valley) are on the southwest side of [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george), where we open first.

## Where you'll find us in Ivins

We're not open for public stops yet, and we won't make up a date. Public stops go on the [homepage stops list](https://thirstybeaches.com/#stops) and the live map once they're actually booked, and text and email alerts are coming soon. Until then, the fastest way to get the trailer to Ivins is to [book it for your own event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Ivins#quote).

# Dirty soda in Hurricane and Sand Hollow, Utah

> A retro dirty soda and soft-serve trailer for Hurricane, LaVerkin and Sand Hollow parties, family reunions and group days on the road to Zion.

Canonical page: https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-hurricane-sand-hollow

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) · Hurricane & Sand Hollow

Opening soon · Booking Hurricane events now


Red sand, warm water and a long drive home. Dirty sodas built to order, real soft-serve floats and fresh espresso for Hurricane parties, Sand Hollow group days and family reunions on the road to Zion, from a retro trailer that comes to you.

[Book a Hurricane Event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Hurricane#quote) [See the Menu](https://thirstybeaches.com/menu)

## The beach town of Washington County

Thirsty Beaches was built around one idea, bringing the beach to you, and Hurricane is the town in Washington County with a beach of its own. Sand Hollow's red-sand shoreline and warm water pull boats, paddleboards and side-by-sides all summer, and Quail Creek is just around the corner. A cold dirty soda or a soft-serve float after a day on the water is exactly the drink we built the trailer for. Utah's best-known chain started here in Washington County, so the soda habit runs deep; what we add is real soft serve and espresso, poured at your party.

## Sand Hollow and Quail Creek: plan it the right way

Utah State Parks require permission (a special use permit) for commercial vendors, so we don't just pull onto the beach and start selling. For a big group day at Sand Hollow, talk to us early and we'll work through what the park needs with you, or we'll meet your group at your rental, a home or a private lot close by. The resort and golf venues near the reservoir run their own food and drinks, so private events there go through the venue first.

## Hurricane, LaVerkin and Toquerville

Hurricane has grown fast, but it still has its old downtown along State Street and a harvest celebration, Peach Days, that goes back generations. Washington County Legacy Park hosts the county fair, rodeos and markets, and county and festival events usually run their own concessions or vendor applications, so we check those first. Across the river bridge, LaVerkin, and up the road Toquerville and Leeds, are small towns with their own history and their own page: [LaVerkin, Toquerville and Leeds](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-laverkin-toquerville-leeds). In Hurricane we do backyard parties, ward activities, Hurricane High booster nights, HOA socials in the newer neighborhoods and [graduation open houses](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party).

## Family reunions and vacation rentals

A lot of families gather in the rentals around Sand Hollow and Hurricane, with a pool, a big yard and three generations under one roof for the week. That's a perfect private booking: we pull up for a couple of hours, pour for everybody, and the cousins talk about the float bar for years. Check your rental's rules on vendors and parking, tell us the head count, and we'll quote it. Further out, like Springdale or the Zion side, ask and we'll put any travel in the quote.

## Trails, off-road weekends and the heat

Hurricane is a base camp for Gooseberry Mesa, the trails along the Hurricane Cliffs and the dunes out by Sand Mountain. Ride groups and off-road weekends start early and end hot. We open the morning with espresso and sweet-cream cold brew, then switch to dirty sodas, lemonades and floats over nugget ice as the day heats up. Summer afternoons here pass 100 degrees, so for a midday event we'll suggest a short menu and a window that keeps the line moving. Event organizers set their own vendor rules, so tell us the event and we'll check first.

## Where you'll find us in Hurricane

We're not open for public stops yet, and we won't make up a date. Public stops go on the [homepage stops list](https://thirstybeaches.com/#stops) and the live map once they're actually booked, and text and email alerts are coming soon. Until then, the fastest way to get the trailer to Hurricane or Sand Hollow is to [book it for your own event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=Hurricane#quote). Planning a reception? See [southern Utah weddings](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-wedding-soda-bar), or head back to [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george).

# Dirty soda in LaVerkin, Toquerville and Leeds, Utah

[Book an Event Up North](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=LaVerkin%2C%20Toquerville%20or%20Leeds#quote) [See the Menu](https://thirstybeaches.com/menu)

## LaVerkin: canals, orchards and the overlook

LaVerkin sits between Hurricane and Toquerville, across the river bridge from Hurricane. It was farmland first, then a surveyed townsite, and the LaVerkin Canal, the LaVerkin Fruit and Nursery Company, the old hot springs at Pah Tempe and the LaVerkin Overlook, with its view across the Hurricane Valley, are all part of the town's story. It is still a small town, and a backyard there is an easy place to park a drink trailer.

## Toquerville: the old town on Ash Creek

Toquerville is about nineteen miles northeast of St. George on State Route 17. Its settlers built near the village of Toquer, the Paiute leader who befriended them, and the town took his name; the Washington County Historical Society says the word means black, for the volcanic mountain the town sits beneath. Toquerville had the first cotton gin in the state, grew fruit in its warm climate and was even a county seat for a while. Today it is a quiet town where a graduation open house or a reunion fills the whole street, and that is the kind of party we built the trailer for.

## Leeds and Silver Reef

Leeds sits along I-15 near exits 22 and 23. It was organized as Bennington and renamed after Leeds, England, where its bishop had served a mission. Its first business was grapes and wine, and then it supplied the nearby mining town of Silver Reef. Leeds passed its own historic preservation ordinance, and the Silver Reef Museum now fills the old Wells Fargo Express building, on a monument site owned by Washington County. Historic sites and museums set their own rules, so an event there goes through them first. A backyard in Leeds is simpler.

## A trailer that brings its own power

Out here the party is often on a big lot, a family property or a ranch-style yard without an outlet anywhere near it. That is fine: the trailer runs on its own generator and carries its own water, so we only need a flat spot that a truck and trailer can pull into. We do backyard receptions, reunions, birthday parties, missionary farewells and homecomings, ward activities and booster nights. These towns are a longer drive from St. George, so we'll include any travel in the quote, and the math works best when there's a crowd.

## Toward Zion and the long summer

Further up the road toward Springdale and Zion, ask and we'll put the drive in the quote. We don't set up inside the national park; we'll meet a group at a home or a rental outside it. Summer afternoons up here pass 100 degrees just like in St. George, so we plan morning events with espresso and sweet-cream cold brew or evening parties with floats and dirty sodas over nugget ice.

## The rest of the county

South across the river, [Hurricane and Sand Hollow](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-hurricane-sand-hollow) have their own page, and so does [Washington City](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-washington-city). [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) is where the trailer opens first. Planning a reception or a family milestone? See [southern Utah weddings](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-wedding-soda-bar) and [graduations and birthdays](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party).

## Where you'll find us up north

We're not open for public stops yet, and we won't make up a date. Public stops go on the [homepage stops list](https://thirstybeaches.com/#stops) and the live map once they're actually booked, and text and email alerts are coming soon. Until then, the fastest way to get the trailer to LaVerkin, Toquerville or Leeds is to [book it for your own event](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=LaVerkin%2C%20Toquerville%20or%20Leeds#quote).

## LaVerkin, Toquerville and Leeds dirty soda FAQ

**Do you come to LaVerkin, Toquerville and Leeds?**

Yes. They're part of Washington County, where we open first. [Send the date, place and head count](https://thirstybeaches.com/utah-dirty-soda-catering?city=LaVerkin%2C%20Toquerville%20or%20Leeds#quote) and we'll reply with a price within one business day.

**Is there a travel charge?**

These towns are a longer drive from St. George, so any travel is included up front in your quote. Bigger groups make the drive pencil out best.

**Do you need power or water?**

No. The trailer runs on its own generator and carries its own water. We just need a flat spot a truck and trailer can pull into.

**Can you set up at Silver Reef or another historic site?**

Only with the site's permission, since museums and historic sites set their own rules. We'll check with them before we quote. A private yard nearby is the simplest option.

**Do you go to Springdale or Zion?**

Ask, and we'll put any travel in the quote. We don't set up inside the national park; we can meet your group at a home or rental outside it.

**When will the trailer be open?**

We're not open for public stops yet, and we won't make up a date. Stops go on the homepage stops list and live map the minute they're booked. Private events are booking now.

Southern Utah weddings

## A St. George reception, done the Utah way

A lot of St. George weddings follow the same rhythm: a sealing or ceremony earlier in the day, a family luncheon, then an evening reception or open house where half the neighborhood comes through the line. Most of those receptions are dry, so the drink bar is the bar. In the town where Utah’s best-known chain started, dirty soda is the obvious pick, and a trailer that pours to order for every guest turns the drink line into part of the party instead of a table of warm cans.

Guests line up for a Thirst Trap (Dr Pepper, coconut, sweet cream) or a Mountain Dew with mango and watermelon. The kids get soft-serve cones, the grandparents get a caffeine-free lemonade, and the photographer gets a neon-pink trailer against a red-rock sky.

## Built for receptions in the heat

Southern Utah’s wedding season runs long. Spring and fall evenings are close to perfect, and summer receptions simply start later, after the sun drops behind the ridge. Every drink is poured over nugget ice, and the soft-serve machine turns any soda into a float, which is hard to beat at a July reception. For daytime summer events we’ll suggest a shorter menu and a time window that keeps the line moving, so nobody in a suit waits long on hot pavement.

## Make it yours

We’ll name a signature drink after the two of you and match the syrups and toppings to your colors, so sage and terracotta or navy and gold both work. Keep the menu to five or six drinks so the rush after the cake moves fast, or open the full board for a long open house. Add espresso for a late dance floor, or sweet-cream cold brew for a morning luncheon.

## Backyards, venues and where the trailer parks

We do backyard receptions in Little Valley, Bloomington and Green Valley, family-property open houses in Washington City and Santa Clara, red-rock patios out in Ivins and Kayenta, and receptions out toward Hurricane and the road to Zion. The trailer needs a flat spot that a truck and trailer can pull into, close enough to your guests that the line feels like part of the party. It runs on its own generator and carries its own water.

One thing to check first: some resort, golf and event venues require all food and drinks to come from their own kitchen. Look at your venue contract or ask your coordinator whether outside food and beverage vendors are allowed. If they are, we’ll work with the coordinator on load-in time and parking before we quote. If your reception is in [Ivins](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-ivins), [Santa Clara](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-santa-clara) or [Hurricane](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-hurricane-sand-hollow), those pages cover the area, and [dirty soda in St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) covers the rest of the county.

## Showers, luncheons, ring ceremonies and open houses

Bridal showers, ring ceremonies, sealing-day luncheons and backyard open houses can use the smaller Sip & Go package: the same trailer, a shorter list and a smaller bill. Missionary-age siblings, cousins from the Wasatch Front and the grandkids all end up at the window, so we always bring kid sizes and zero-sugar versions.

## Before you book

**Can you name a drink after us?**

Yes. Tell us what the two of you love, and we’ll build a signature drink, match it to your colors and put your names on it for the night.

**How many guests can you serve at a big St. George reception?**

Every drink is built to order, so for a reception of a few hundred guests we’ll recommend a short menu and the right number of hours. Put your head count in the form and we’ll plan around it.

**Can you serve at our venue in Ivins, Kayenta or Hurricane?**

If the venue allows outside food and beverage vendors, yes. Some resort and event venues require everything from their own kitchen, so check your contract first. Backyards and family property are the easiest.

**What about a summer reception?**

Start after the heat breaks if you can. We pour over nugget ice, soft-serve floats are the favorite, and we’ll suggest a menu and a time window that keep the line short.

**Can guests pay for their own drinks?**

Most couples cover everyone, but you can also set a cap and switch to guests paying after that. Tell us which you want in the form.

**How far ahead should we book?**

For a Saturday reception, the sooner the better. A month or more out is ideal. For a shower or a weeknight open house, ask anyway: if the trailer is free, we’ll come.

Tournaments & team parties

## St. George is a tournament town

When the Wasatch Front is cold, teams come south. St. George’s fields and courts fill up through the cooler months with softball and baseball, soccer and lacrosse, pickleball and youth mountain biking, and families drive down from Salt Lake, Las Vegas and Arizona to spend the weekend on the sidelines. The Fields at Little Valley, the Canyons Softball Complex and the trail park in Desert Color are the kind of places where a cold drink between games is worth a lot.

That’s the crowd we built the trailer for. Parents at a 7 a.m. first game want an iced latte. Players want a float after the last out. Little siblings want anything blue. We pour all of it to order from one retro trailer.

## For tournament directors and complex managers

The simplest setup is a pop-up where families buy their own drinks, so it costs your event nothing. The trailer runs on its own generator and carries its own water, so we don’t need a hookup. Tell us what your venue requires, such as a vendor application, a certificate of insurance or a health permit, and we’ll confirm we can meet it before we quote. Some complexes have their own concession stand or an exclusive vendor; we’ll check that first, and we won’t set up next to your stand without your say-so.

We only post a public stop once it’s actually booked, so if you’d like the trailer at your tournament, get in touch early and we’ll work out the details with you and the venue.

## Team parties after the last game

End-of-season parties, a post-tournament celebration at a park pavilion, a team dinner in a backyard, a coaches’ thank-you. The team or the club covers a tab (all of it, or up to a set amount), we park, and every player gets a drink their way. Floats and soft-serve cones tend to win. We have kid sizes for the younger teams and zero-sugar sodas for the parents keeping count.

## Booster club and team fundraisers

Raising money for a travel season, new uniforms or a team trip? Ask about a fundraiser stop: we park at your event, families buy their own drinks, and part of the sales goes back to your team or booster club. Put “fundraiser” in the form and we’ll send the details.

## What we need at the field

A flat spot a truck and trailer can pull into, close to where families walk between fields but out of the fire lanes and the parking aisles. We arrive well before the first game, set up the ordering kiosk and the window, and pack out after the last one, leaving the spot clean. If the venue wants us in a particular lot or behind a particular backstop, tell us when you send the details and we’ll plan around it.

## Early games, hot afternoons

Tournament days in St. George can start cold and end hot. We open the morning with espresso and sweet-cream cold brew, then switch to dirty sodas, lemonades and floats as the day warms up, all over nugget ice. Caffeine-free lemonades and Italian sodas are on every menu. One honest note: a dirty soda is a treat, not a sports drink, so keep the water jugs on the bench. More about the trailer and the rest of the county on [dirty soda in St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george).

Church & school events

## Ward parties, youth nights and homecomings

Washington County’s calendar is full of church activities: ward parties and Christmas parties, Pioneer Day picnics, trunk-or-treats, youth nights, youth conferences, trek send-offs, and the missionary farewells and homecomings that bring the whole family to one backyard. A drink trailer turns any of them into an event people talk about, and in the town where Utah’s best-known chain started, a dirty soda is the treat everybody already wants.

If your activity is at a meetinghouse, the building’s rules come first, so ask your bishopric or building representative before you book. A covered tab with no sales is usually the simplest fit. If the building isn’t an option, a park pavilion, a school lot or a member’s driveway works just as well.

## An activity menu a bishopric can approve

We’ll put together a short, family-friendly menu that a bishopric, a Young Women or Young Men presidency, or an activities committee can sign off on quickly. It can be fully caffeine-free: lemonades, Italian sodas, caffeine-free soda bases and soft-serve cones. Zero-sugar versions and kid sizes come standard. Set a budget and we’ll cap the tab at it, so the ward clerk knows the number before the night starts.

## Schools across Washington County

PTA carnivals, back-to-school nights, teacher appreciation week, senior nights, and band, choir and drill banquets. PTAs, PTOs and booster clubs can book us at any school in the county, from Desert Hills, Snow Canyon, Pine View, Dixie and Crimson Cliffs to Hurricane, plus the elementary and middle schools that feed them. Schools and the district set their own rules for vendors on campus, so tell us what yours needs and we’ll work through it before we quote.

Few things say thank you to a southern Utah teacher like a dirty soda on a Friday afternoon. Pick the morning or the afternoon, we park at the school and pour for the staff, and the PTA covers the tab. Need an invoice or a purchase order? Ask in the notes.

## Farewells and homecomings

A missionary farewell or homecoming open house brings out the whole ward, the cousins and the high school friends, usually all at once. Park the trailer in the driveway and the line becomes part of the party. We can name a drink after the missionary or the mission, keep the menu short so the line moves while the family greets people at the door, and put everyone on one tab so nobody has to dig for a wallet.

## Utah Tech students and student wards

On campus, food and drink usually go through the university’s own dining and event services, so check with them first for anything held at Utah Tech. Off campus, student wards, clubs, intramural teams and apartment complexes book us directly for socials, back-to-school nights and finals-week study breaks.

## Fundraisers

Raising money for a class trip, a youth trek, a team or a cause? Ask about a fundraiser stop: we park at your event, guests buy their own drinks, and part of the sales goes back to your group. Fundraisers where guests pay work best at a school, a park or a business lot. Put “fundraiser” in the form and we’ll send the details. More about the trailer and the rest of the county on [dirty soda in St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george).

Questions

## Before you book

**Can we leave caffeine off the menu?**

Yes. Tell us in the form and we’ll build a caffeine-free menu from lemonades, Italian sodas, caffeine-free soda bases and soft serve.

**Can you come to an activity at the church building?**

Ask your bishopric or building representative about the meetinghouse rules first. A covered tab with no sales is usually the simplest fit. If the building isn’t an option, a park pavilion or a member’s home works well.

**Can the ward, school or PTA pay by invoice?**

Ask in the notes and we’ll work out what your ward, school or organization needs when we send the quote.

**Do you do fundraisers?**

Yes. Guests buy their own drinks and part of the sales goes back to your group. Fundraisers work best at a school, a park or a business lot. Mention it in the form and we’ll share how it works.

**Can you serve at Utah Tech?**

On campus, check with the university’s dining and event services first, since they usually handle food and drink there. Off campus, student wards, clubs and apartment complexes can book us directly.

**Do you have kid sizes?**

Yes. The Beach Babies menu is sized and priced for kids, and soft-serve cones are always a hit at Primary and youth activities.

# Dirty soda for St. George graduation and birthday parties

> A dirty soda and soft-serve trailer for St. George graduation open houses, kids' birthdays, milestone parties and family reunions. Booking now.

Canonical page: https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) · Graduations & birthdays

Now taking event requests


Graduation open houses, kids’ birthdays, milestone parties and family reunions across Washington County. A retro trailer with dirty sodas, soft-serve floats and espresso, and a drink named for the guest of honor.

[Get a Quote](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party#quote) [See Packages](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party#packages)

- Reply in 1 business day
- 114-drink menu, or your short list
- Zero-sugar & kid sizes
- Drink named for the guest of honor

Graduations & birthdays

## Graduation open houses, the southern Utah way

Graduation in Washington County usually means an open house: the grad in the driveway, a slideshow on the garage door, and the ward, the cousins and the whole team dropping by over a couple of hours. That drop-in rhythm is exactly what a drink trailer is good at. Guests walk up, order a drink their way, and stay to talk instead of grabbing a can and leaving. We do open houses for graduates from Desert Hills, Dixie, Pine View, Snow Canyon, Crimson Cliffs, Hurricane and the other high schools across the county, plus college grads from Utah Tech and Dixie Technical College.

We’ll name a drink after the graduate and match the syrups to the school colors, and keep the menu short so the line moves when the crowd arrives all at once. Graduation open houses tend to land on the same few weekends, so book as early as you can.

## Birthdays for every age

Kids’ birthdays are the easy ones: Beach Babies kid sizes, soft-serve cones and anything blue. Sweet sixteens and eighteenths get the full board and a drink named for the birthday. Then there are the milestone birthdays: a fiftieth with the neighbors, an eightieth with four generations in the backyard, a surprise party at a rental house. The grandparents can have a caffeine-free lemonade or a Diet Coke with coconut, and the toddlers get a cone.

## Family milestones

The parties St. George families throw don’t stop at birthdays. Baptism-day lunches, baby showers, anniversaries, retirement parties, family reunions, and the missionary farewells and homecomings that bring the whole family to one backyard (see [church and school events](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-church-school-events)). Bridal showers and receptions have their own page: [southern Utah weddings](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-wedding-soda-bar).

## Where the trailer parks

Most of these parties happen at home, and that is the easiest setup. We need a flat spot that a truck and trailer can pull into, like a driveway, a side yard or the curb out front, close enough to your guests that the line feels like part of the party. The trailer runs on its own generator and carries its own water. If your neighborhood has an HOA, check its rules on vendors and street parking. A party that spills into a public street or uses a city park beyond a normal reservation can need a St. George special event permit, and the city asks for those applications at least 45 days ahead; park reservations go through City Parks. Washington City, Santa Clara, Ivins and Hurricane have their own rules. More on [HOA and neighborhood parties](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party).

## How the tab works

Most families cover everyone. You can also set a cap, cover the first drink, or let guests buy their own after that. Tell us the head count and how long the open house runs, and we’ll suggest the right package and a menu that fits your crowd. More about the trailer on [dirty soda in St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george).

## Open houses in the heat

Graduation and summer birthdays land in the hottest part of the year, when afternoons regularly pass 100 degrees. Evening open houses work best, after the sun drops. Every drink is poured over nugget ice, and a soft-serve float is hard to beat on a hot night. For a midday party we’ll suggest a short menu and a shaded spot for the line.

## Before you book

**Can you come to a graduation open house?**

Yes. Open houses are one of the parties we built the trailer for. Send the date, the address area, the head count and how long the open house runs, and we’ll reply with a price within one business day.

**How far ahead should we book for graduation?**

As early as you can, since graduation open houses tend to land on the same few weekends. For a birthday or a weeknight party, ask anyway: if the trailer is free, we’ll come.

**Do you have kid sizes for a kids’ birthday?**

Yes. The Beach Babies menu is sized and priced for kids, and soft-serve cones are always a hit. Caffeine-free drinks are easy too.

Yes. Most families cover everyone, but you can set a cap or cover the first drink and let guests buy their own after that.

**Can you name a drink after the graduate?**

# Dirty soda for St. George HOA and neighborhood parties

> A dirty soda and soft-serve trailer for St. George HOA socials, block parties, pool openings, 55+ clubhouse nights and apartment resident events.

Canonical page: https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) · HOA & neighborhood parties

Now taking event requests


Pool openings, block parties, clubhouse socials and 55+ community nights across Washington County. A retro trailer with dirty sodas, soft-serve floats and espresso, and the tab handled however your HOA wants.

[Get a Quote](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party#quote) [See Packages](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party#packages)

- Reply in 1 business day
- 114-drink menu, or your short list
- Zero-sugar & kid sizes
- Own power & water

HOA & neighborhood parties

## A town of neighborhoods with a social calendar

A lot of St. George lives in neighborhoods with an HOA, a clubhouse and a calendar to fill: pool openings, movie nights, holiday parties, back-to-school bashes and welcome parties for the new move-ins. That is an old tradition here. When The Park at Green Valley opened, it came with an owners association, a clubhouse and a pool, which the Washington County Historical Society counts among the firsts for St. George. Today Desert Color runs summer kickoffs with food trucks and dive-in movie nights, and neighborhoods like Kayenta have homeowners associations of their own.

A drink trailer is the easiest crowd-pleaser on that calendar. We park at the clubhouse lot or the common area, pour every drink to order over nugget ice, and the whole street gets a drink built the way they like it. Real soft serve turns any soda into a float, and the kids get Beach Babies sizes and cones.

## 55+ communities and clubhouse socials

St. George’s active-adult communities run some of the busiest social calendars in town. SunRiver, the first 55+ community in southern Utah, has a community center of more than 35,000 square feet with a ballroom, over 70 clubs and groups, and its own poolside café, so the association sets the rules for vendors on its grounds, and a club or committee would go through it first. Desert Color has a 55+ neighborhood too. For an afternoon social, a club party or a street get-together with the association’s OK, we bring zero-sugar sodas, caffeine-free lemonades and Italian sodas, and floats that remind everybody of the soda fountain they grew up with.

## How HOA billing works

The HOA can cover everyone, set a cap, or let residents buy their own. A pop-up where neighbors pay costs the HOA nothing. One quote, one invoice if you need it, and a clear price your board can approve. Tell us what your HOA or management company requires from vendors and we’ll confirm we can meet it before we quote.

## Clubhouse lot, common area or the street?

A clubhouse parking lot or a common area the HOA controls is the simplest spot: you approve it, and we need a flat place a truck and trailer can pull into, close to your guests. The trailer runs on its own generator and carries its own water, so no hookup is needed. A party that spills into a public street or uses a city park beyond a normal reservation can need a St. George special event permit, and the city asks for those applications at least 45 days ahead; park reservations go through City Parks. Washington City, Santa Clara, Ivins and Hurricane have their own rules.

## Apartments and townhome communities

Resident appreciation nights, pool-season kickoffs, move-in welcome events and leasing open houses work the same way, with the property manager covering the tab or residents buying their own. We follow your community’s rules on where to park and when to load in.

## Neighborhood pages

See the page for your part of town: [Desert Color](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-desert-color), [Bloomington and Green Valley](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-bloomington-green-valley), [Washington City](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-washington-city) and Coral Canyon, [Santa Clara](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-santa-clara), [Ivins](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-ivins) and Kayenta, and [Hurricane](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-hurricane-sand-hollow). Throwing a birthday or a graduation open house for your own family? See [graduations and birthdays](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-graduation-birthday-party), or start at [dirty soda in St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george).

## Before you book

**Can the HOA cover everyone’s drinks?**

**Do we need a permit for a block party?**

If the party stays on HOA common area or private property, your HOA’s rules apply. A party in a public street or a city park beyond a normal reservation can need a St. George special event permit, applied for at least 45 days ahead. Other cities have their own rules.

Yes. Most sodas come in a zero-sugar version, lemonades and Italian sodas have no caffeine, and kid sizes and soft-serve cones cover the youngest neighbors.

# Dirty soda for St. George company parties

> A dirty soda, soft-serve and espresso trailer for St. George employee appreciation days, shift-change treats, open houses and summer company parties.

[Thirsty Beaches](https://thirstybeaches.com/) · [St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george) · Company parties

Employee appreciation, shift-change treats, customer open houses and summer parties across Washington County. A retro trailer pouring dirty sodas, soft serve and espresso, with the tab handled however you want.

- Reply in 1 business day
- 114-drink menu, or your short list
- Zero-sugar & kid sizes
- Custom company drink

Company parties

## The office soda run, for the whole team at once

In St. George the afternoon soda run is practically a workplace tradition: somebody takes a list, drives to a drive-thru and comes back with a tray of drinks that are already watering down. A drink trailer does it the other way around. We park in your lot, everyone walks out and orders their own, built to order over nugget ice, and the whole team takes a break together. In the town where Utah’s best-known chain started, a dirty soda is the thank-you people actually want.

We add the two things a drive-thru can’t: real soft serve, so any soda can become a float, and espresso pulled to order for iced lattes and sweet-cream cold brew. Zero-sugar sodas, caffeine-free lemonades and Italian sodas cover the people who are counting.

## Built for the way St. George works

A lot of St. George doesn’t work nine to five. Hospital and clinic teams run around the clock, the school district and the university have their own calendars, an airline is headquartered here, and tech companies have moved into Tech Ridge, on the site of the old municipal airport. Add dealerships, builders and construction crews, resorts, hotels and shops. Every one of them has an employee appreciation week, a goal that got hit, or a summer party that needs something better than a sheet cake.

## Shift changes and night crews

For teams that work around the clock, one visit can catch two shifts. We can open early with espresso and cold brew for the crew coming off nights, then pour sodas and floats for the day shift, or split the visit into two windows on the same day so nobody gets left out. Tell us your shift times in the form and we’ll plan around them. Hospitals, plants and other secure sites usually have their own rules about where a vendor can park; we’ll follow whatever your facilities team sets.

## Customer appreciation and open houses

Grand openings, model-home weekends, dealership sales events, client open houses and customer appreciation days all draw a crowd that lingers if there’s something cold in hand. The company can cover every drink, cover the first round, or let guests buy their own. You’ll need the property owner’s OK for the spot. A party that spills into a public street or uses a city park beyond a normal reservation can need a St. George special event permit, and the city asks for those applications at least 45 days ahead; park reservations go through City Parks. Washington City, Santa Clara, Ivins and Hurricane have their own rules.

## Conventions, expos and team weekends

Conferences, expos and company retreats come with rules of their own. Convention centers and resorts often run their own food and drinks, so we check the venue’s rules first; if outside vendors are allowed, we’ll work with the event team on load-in and parking. A booth crew, a team tent or an after-party at a rental house nearby is usually simpler.

## Put your brand on it

We’ll name a custom drink after your company, your product or your team and match it to your colors. Keep the menu to a short list so a big crowd moves quickly. Need an invoice or a purchase order? Ask in the notes and we’ll set up billing your company can work with when we send the quote. More on [community events](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-hoa-neighborhood-party), [team sponsorship nights](https://thirstybeaches.com/st-george-tournaments-team-parties) and [dirty soda in St. George](https://thirstybeaches.com/dirty-soda-st-george).

Questions

## Before you book

**Can the company cover everyone’s drinks?**

Yes. Cover the whole team, set a cap, or switch to guests paying once the tab runs out. Tell us which you want in the form.

**Can you visit twice in one day for different shifts?**

Often, yes. Put your shift times in the notes and we’ll quote one longer window or two shorter ones, so the night crew and the day crew both get a drink.

**Can you send an invoice?**

Mention it in the notes and we’ll set up billing your company can work with, including a purchase order if you need one, when we send the quote.

**Do you do morning events?**

Yes. We pull espresso to order, so iced lattes and sweet-cream cold brew are ready for a morning all-hands, an open house or a client breakfast.

**What do you need at our building?**

A flat spot a truck and trailer can pull into, close to the door, and the property owner’s OK. The trailer runs on its own generator and carries its own water. If your facility has vendor rules, tell us and we’ll follow them.

**Can we name a drink after our company?**

Yes. We’ll build a custom drink in your colors and name it for your company, product or team.

Tell us the basics and we’ll reply within one business day with availability and a price. No deposit, no obligation.

## What's a dirty soda, and why Naples needs one

A dirty soda is a fountain soda over nugget ice with flavored syrup, maybe fruit purée, and a pour of cream. It's Utah's signature drink, and most of Naples hasn't tried one. That makes it a crowd-pleaser at a party: nobody's seen it before, and everyone wants a second. The classic is our Thirst Trap (Dr Pepper, coconut, sweet cream). From there it's 114 drinks on the board, or [build your own](https://thirstybeaches.com/#build) and show us the screen.

## Soft serve and espresso on the same trailer

One window, three things: dirty sodas, real soft serve and fresh espresso. Turn any soda into a float, hand the kids a cone, and give the coffee crowd an iced latte or sweet-cream cold brew. Zero-sugar versions of most sodas make it easy for guests watching their sugar.

## Built for Naples community and private events

Naples runs on community events, so that's what we built the trailer for: HOA and country-club socials, clubhouse and pool parties, grandkids' visits during the holidays, wedding receptions, private parties, school and church events, and office treat days. You can cover the drinks, open a tab, or let guests buy their own. Season fills up from November to April, so book early for winter weekends. ## Naples dirty soda FAQ

**Is there a dirty soda trailer in Naples, Florida?**

Yes. Thirsty Beaches is a retro dirty soda trailer serving Naples, Bonita Springs, Estero and Marco Island, with soft serve and espresso on the same truck. We're booking events now.

**Can you come to our HOA, clubhouse or country club event?**

Yes. Community socials and pool parties are one of the best fits for the trailer. Many communities require vendors to be approved or insured, so tell us the community when you [ask for a quote](https://thirstybeaches.com/florida-dirty-soda-catering?city=Naples#quote) and we'll send what they need.

**Where did dirty soda come from?**

Utah. Drive-thru soda shops there started mixing syrups, fruit purées and cream into fountain sodas around 2010, and it spread from there. It's still rare in Southwest Florida, which is half the fun.

**Is there something for guests who don't want soda?**

Plenty: soft-serve cones and cups, shakes, fresh espresso drinks, shaken lemonades and creamy Italian sodas, plus kid sizes.

**How far ahead should I book during season?**

Season (roughly November to April) is when Naples calendars fill up. For holiday parties, weddings and big community events, reach out a month or more ahead. For smaller gatherings, ask anyway.

**Do you travel to Fort Myers or Marco Island?**

Yes. Fort Myers, Estero, Bonita Springs and Marco Island are all in range, and travel is included in your quote.

## Tampa Bay dirty soda FAQ

**Is there a dirty soda trailer in Tampa Bay?**

Yes. Thirsty Beaches is a retro dirty soda trailer serving Tampa, St. Pete, Clearwater and the rest of the bay area, with soft serve and espresso on the same truck. We're booking events now.

**Is dirty soda the same as an Italian soda?**

Close cousins. An Italian soda is sparkling water with syrup and cream. A dirty soda uses a real fountain soda (Dr Pepper, Coke, Sprite, Mountain Dew) as the base instead. We pour both.

**Can you cater a wedding or party in Tampa or St. Pete?**

Yes. Receptions, showers, office parties, HOA socials, school and church events. [Send the date, place and head count](https://thirstybeaches.com/florida-dirty-soda-catering?city=Tampa%20Bay#quote) and we'll reply with a price within one business day.

**Can you set up at Clearwater Beach or St. Pete Beach?**

The trailer needs a flat, firm spot it can be driven to, so we set up in a lot, a driveway or a venue pad near the sand rather than on it. Beach parks and venues may need a vendor permit, so tell us the spot when you ask for a quote.

**Can you serve a big crowd, like a school carnival or company picnic?**

Yes. For big crowds we suggest a short menu of crowd favorites so the line moves fast, and we'll size the setup to your head count in the quote.

**How far around the bay will you travel?**

Tampa, St. Pete, Clearwater, Dunedin, Largo, Brandon, Riverview, Wesley Chapel and Apollo Beach are all in range. Further out, ask and we'll quote the drive.
